newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-PORTUGAL'S PRESIDENT STEPS INTO DRUGS ROW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PORTUGAL'S PRESIDENT STEPS INTO DRUGS ROW.

text.p: Portugal's President Jorge Sampaio stepped into a legal battle between soccer authorities and a television station on Wednesday, calling for a full probe into charges that players had smoked hashish before an international game.
Sampaio said the allegations, made by private TV channel SIC, needed to be investigated fully to remove any suspicions which could damage the country's most popular sport.
"It needs a proper investigation by the various entities, whether sporting bodies or eventually judicial authorities, in order to establish the facts," he told journalists.
The president appeared to contradict claims by Portugal's soccer federation that the alleged incidents, dating from November 1995, had been fully probed and shown to be false.
The charges are the latest in a series of scandals which have rocked Portuguese soccer.
The federation announced on Tuesday that it was taking the television station to court over the charges made in a programme on Friday.
SIC interviewed a Brazilian prostitute, identified only as "Paula", who said that she had gone to a party at the players' hotel with some friends and that hashish had been smoked.
She said that she had needed hospital treatment after the party because some of the players had become violent.

Reigning Portuguese champions Porto, some of whose players were alleged to have been involved in the incidents before a European championship game with Ireland, have already said that they are taking legal action over the programme.
Portugal won the match 3-0 and went on to reach the quarter-finals of Euro 96 in England last June.
The federation said the allegations had been investigated and dismissed as untrue when they first surfaced in a newspaper in December 1995.
It added that neither the management of the hotel where the players stayed nor a security firm employed there at the time had reported any unusual activity.
But Sampaio rejected suggestions that there was nothing left to investigate.
"It is not possible to continue in this atmosphere. We need to establish facts...and act on that basis," he said.
